title: Deliberately failing cases: the scorer catches a known incorrect result
process: fault injection through the real benchmark code
boundaryConditions: X1-b adds an inflow of 0.001 m^3/s into T1 for the first hour, which the books are not told about
geometry: as PV-U1 (rectangular b 3 m, S 0.001, n 0.02, Q 3) and PV-C1-a

nFactor.unit: - (the n written into the SWMM input, against the reference's)

leakM3s.unit: m^3/s for 1 h (3.6 m^3, 0.72 % of the system)

reference.independence: the reference keeps the true inputs; only the solver input is faulted

outputs: the status the scorer gives each faulted row, against the expected 'Failed'
criteriaNotes: each fault is sized to fail its criterion by a clear margin: n x 1.25 moves normal depth by about +14 % (against 0.5 %); 3.6 m^3 is 0.72 % of the system volume (against 0.1 %). A faulted row that is not Failed is a scorer defect.
limitations: two faults only: a wrong parameter and a hidden source; more fault classes (a wrong reference, a units error) later
scoring: automated; counted apart from the physics (tally().deliberateFaults)

criteriaRevisions.why: first registration, before the first run
